courses: Course 2 · Data, AI & Regulation in Finance
subtitle: Investments in fintech, digital assets and AI in finance
intro: Designed for acting and aspiring equity analysts who wish to explore investments in fintech, digital assets and AI in finance — combining lectures, expert interviews and home assignments with student project presentations.

modules.title: Financial Institution Business Models
modules.desc: Value chains by vertical: payments, credit, capital markets and insurance.

modules.title: Blockchain & Digital Assets
modules.desc: How tokens, settlement and custody reshape financial primitives.

modules.title: Consumer Sentiment & Product Expectations
modules.desc: The demand side of fintech — surveys, behavioural signals and product fit.

modules.title: Fintech Investable Universe
modules.desc: PE and VC holdings, ETF composition, public-company valuation and M&A dynamics.

modules.title: Data and AI in Finance
modules.desc: Markets for financial data and where AI applications create real value in the industry.

modules.title: Policy & Regulation
modules.desc: Implications for policy, regulation and the durability of fintech business models.

outcomes: Value a fintech company from its annual report end-to-end
Build a thesis-driven fintech portfolio across verticals
Identify AI applications most likely to reshape finance
Communicate fintech investment ideas to investment committees
audience: Investors wanting deeper fintech and digital-asset coverage

instructors.name: FinTech Lead
instructors.bio: Career equity research across fintech and digital assets.

faqs.a: "Your Fintech Investment Targets" — three companies you would invest in, your reasoning, what allocations to avoid, and the fintech investor you admire most. 400–500 words, no LLM-generated submissions accepted.
10–20 hours per week of lectures, self-study and project work.
